title: Get API keys
text: Access Elsevier developer portal : https://dev.elsevier.com/ Click “want API key” Sign institutional/organisation credentials Click “Create API key” Enter label API key (avoid use spaces name) don’t need provide website URL Read API Service Agreement Tick “agree API Service Agreement” Read text data mining provisions Tick “agree TDM Provisions” Click “Submit” redirected “API Key” find API key institutional Scopus subscriptions also require institutional token (insttoken) addition API key. API calls return authentication error (HTTP 401) even valid key, contact Elsevier support request institutional token account. key works , need institutional token.

title: Get API keys
text: Access Clarivate developer portal : https://developer.clarivate.com/ Click log already member, sign using institutional/organisation credentials Click “Applications” top page Enter application ID (avoid use spaces name) Enter application name Enter application description explain use API (e.g., running systematic review dog vaccine) Choose client type “Confidential: Server side application, can keep secrets confidential tick “application use OAuth2.0 Flows (Client Credentials flow, .e. using redirects)” Click “Register application” Click “APIs” top page Select tile “Web Science API Expanded” bottom page click “Subscribe” need wait Clarivate approve application provide individual API key (can take several days weeks, hesitate contact Clarivate support team updates ts.support.anz@clarivate.com) Well done! Now got API keys, can continue next tutorial → LitFetchR (Tutorial)

title: LitFetchR 1.0.0
text: CRAN release: 2026-06-18 Major reworking retrieval pipeline, consolidating series performance, reliability, data-quality improvements. exported function interface unchanged apart two new optional arguments save_api_keys() (scp_insttoken ncbi_api_key), returned data frame changed (see “Output columns” ).

title: LitFetchR 1.0.0
text: issue column renamed number. Code referred output column name issue must updated. Added pages isbn columns output three extractors. returned data frame now consistent 12 columns across Web Science, Scopus, PubMed: author, year, title, journal, volume, number, abstract, doi, pages, isbn, source, platform_id.

title: LitFetchR 1.0.0
text: Web Science Scopus extractors longer make individual per-record API calls. metadata now extracted directly batch search responses, greatly reducing number API requests time per run. PubMed record details now fetched batches 200 PMIDs per call instead one call per record. Replaced row--row rbind accumulation list collection single combine three extractors. Removed redundant save--reread history_id.xlsx extraction.

title: LitFetchR 1.0.0
text: Scopus API key now sent X-ELS-APIKey request header instead URL query parameter, matching Elsevier’s current requirements. Added optional support Scopus institutional token. Set save_api_keys(scp_insttoken = "..."); present sent X-ELS-Insttoken header Scopus requests. institutional subscriptions require . save_api_keys() can now save optional NCBI/PubMed API key save_api_keys(ncbi_api_key = "..."), enables higher PubMed request rate. Previously key added .Renviron hand.

title: LitFetchR 1.0.0
text: Rate-limit responses (HTTP 429) now retried dedicated loop respects Retry-header. Authentication failures (HTTP 401/403) now fail immediately clear diagnostic message instead retrying. Every request now 60-second timeout. PubMed requests now respect NCBI rate limits, using faster rate optional ncbi_api_key environment variable set. create_save_search() now uses retrying HTTP helper extractors rather bare requests. list already-seen record IDs now saved extraction succeeds, interrupted run longer marks records fetched. Search strings containing = now parsed correctly search_list.txt. Fixed handling searches return zero results three extractors.

title: LitFetchR 1.0.0
text: Superscript/subscript markup (<sup>/<inf> tags) now stripped Scopus Web Science titles abstracts preserving content (e.g. 10<sup>2</sup> becomes 102), matching Scopus’ export format. Bare < > used mathematical operators (e.g. p < 0.05) preserved. Web Science extraction now handles record types correctly: DIIDW patents (inventors, year, Derwent abstract), multi-language abstracts CSCD/KJD/SCIELO (preferring English variant), BCI/ZOOREC book-chapter journal titles. Italic terms CABI titles abstracts reconstructed place, article URL used fallback DOI available.

title: LitFetchR 1.0.0
text: Per-run timestamped sheets history files replaced append-log sheets, keeping single growing record instead one sheet per run.
